chapters.summary: Paul gives thanks for the Colossian believers and sets forth the supremacy of Christ and his work of redemption, urging them to hold fast to the true faith.
keyPoints: Paul gives thanks to God for the Colossians' faith, love, and hope, because the gospel is bearing fruit and growing among them.
Paul prays that believers would be filled with spiritual wisdom and power, so that they may walk worthy of the Lord and bear fruit in every good work.
Paul explains that Christ is the creator and sustainer of all things, that the church is his body, and that through the cross he made peace, reconciling believers to God.
chapters.application: Let us always maintain a thankful heart, pray for the growth of fellow believers, and give Christ first place in our lives, living out the fruit of the gospel, reconciled to God and at peace with one another.

chapters.summary: Paul urges the Colossian believers to be rooted and built up in Christ, warning them against human philosophy and man-made regulations, because the whole fullness of God dwells in Christ.
keyPoints: Paul labors earnestly for the church, that their hearts may be encouraged, knit together in love, and come to the full riches of understanding in knowing the mystery of Christ.
He warns believers not to be taken captive by fine-sounding arguments and human tradition, for in Christ all the fullness of deity dwells in bodily form.
In Christ, believers received a circumcision not performed by human hands; they died and were raised with Christ, and are no longer under the bondage of regulations and rituals.
chapters.application: Let us be rooted and built up in Christ, holding him as the head, refusing to follow human traditions and the elemental principles of the world, and live out the true freedom we have in him.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to set their minds on things above, to put off the old self and put on the new, and to live out Christ's love and unity in daily life.
keyPoints: Seek the things above and set your mind on Christ, not on earthly things.
Put to death whatever belongs to your earthly nature - sexual immorality, greed, and the like - for these bring on the wrath of God.
Clothe yourselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, forgiving one another, and above all bind these together with love, which is the bond of perfect unity.
themes: Putting the Old Self to Death
chapters.application: Today, let us lay aside selfishness and anger, have the mind of Christ, treat our family and neighbors with gentleness and love, and glorify God in everything we do.

chapters.summary: Paul urges believers to devote themselves to prayer, staying watchful and thankful, and to pray that God would open a door for the message. He also teaches how to conduct themselves toward outsiders, and closes with greetings and instructions.
keyPoints: Believers are urged to devote themselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful, and to pray that God would open a door for the gospel.
Believers are taught to walk in wisdom toward outsiders, and to let their speech always be seasoned with grace.
Paul instructs Tychicus and Onesimus to carry news to the church, and sends greetings to the saints.
chapters.application: In the busyness of life, devote yourself to prayer and seize every opportunity to share the gospel. In conversation, speak with gentleness and wisdom, so that God's name may be glorified.
